implication: Once a CIRP is admitted by NCLT, the board and management are superseded by a court-appointed insolvency professional; creditor committees control the resolution plan; and all pre-insolvency claims are frozen - critical for lenders, suppliers and shareholders tracking recovery timelines.

headline: CMI Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: CMI Limited has informed NSE of initiation of a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), triggering the formal IBC framework for resolution or liquidation of the company's debts and assets.
detail: CMI Limited's entry into CIRP indicates either an admission of insolvency petition by the NCLT Bench or the company's notification to the stock exchange of such admission. Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, CIRP typically runs for 180 days (extendable by 90 days) during which a resolution professional is appointed to manage the company, a creditor committee is formed, and a resolution plan is invited from interested parties. The process culminates in either adoption of a resolution plan (transferring the company or its assets) or initiation of liquidation. Specific creditor claims, debt quantum and resolution professional identity remain undisclosed in the NSE notification alone.
